note: Corrections to the league Obvibase register, applied by scripts/build_trade_counts.py at read time. The register is the league's and is re-exported from time to time; hand-editing a derived file would be undone by the next export and would leave no record of what changed. Each entry names the register row by its own id and says what is wrong with it. `drop` removes the row from every count and every price; `set` rewrites fields. A row whose id is absent from a future export is reported, not silently skipped. A correction names its source only where that source is content to be named: this repository is public and the league reads it, so a manager is never put in a file for having answered a question.

corrections.why: The row has one side. It records The Machines sending Travis Kelce, a 2027 second and Ben Sinnott, with nothing entered coming back, on the league's draft day -- nine entries deep, the busiest page in the register and the likeliest place for a row to be opened and never finished. A reading of what came the other way was offered and could not be confirmed. An unconfirmed trade is not one this desk will count, price or publish, so the row is dropped from everything. It is recorded here, in full, so it can be restored the moment somebody can say for certain what came back and from whom.
corrections.source: Withheld at the source's request. The desk holds it.
corrections.effect: The Machines read 13 deals in 2025 rather than 14, and the register agrees with the itemised ledger on all sixteen franchises in all five seasons.
